contents.name: §2.2 graded finite-module and finite-projective categories
Equations (2.3)–(2.4), Laurent action by internal shift
§2.2 homogeneous Hom and sesquilinear Cartan pairing
contents.reason: The survey supplies the homogeneous-Hom and q-dimension convention and states sesquilinearity under its algebraically closed-field setup; this item proves descent and the shift exponent locally over an arbitrary field.

contents.name: Equation (2.5), homogeneous decomposition of Hom for finite-dimensional modules
contents.reason: This item uses homogeneous Hom spaces and derives the needed finite support directly; it does not claim that full ungraded Hom equals the direct sum of homogeneous Hom spaces.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1, radical of a finitely generated graded module is graded
contents.reason: The local graded-cover and simple-head arguments use minimal graded projective summands and superfluous kernels; no general graded-radical theorem is needed.

contents.name: Lemma 2.2, graded irreducibles remain irreducible after forgetting the grading
contents.reason: The pair proves bases for graded isomorphism and shift orbits internally; comparison with ungraded irreducibility is not needed for its Cartan pairing.

contents.name: Lemma 2.3, gradability of each ordinary simple module
contents.reason: The local finite orbit proof classifies graded simples as quotients of shifts of the regular graded module; it makes no claim that every ordinary simple is gradable.

contents.name: §2.2 graded composition multiplicity polynomial
§2.2 shift and homogeneous-Hom conventions for the graded dual-number example
contents.reason: Kleshchev supplies the internal-shift and homogeneous-Hom convention; the dual-number normal form, graded-simple orbit, projective cover, and Cartan polynomial are derived locally.

contents.name: §2.2 homogeneous-Hom and Cartan-pairing conventions for the nonsplit-field example
contents.reason: Kleshchev supplies only the homogeneous-Hom and pairing conventions; the division-ring simple/projective classification, the finite-length small-abelian verification, and the real dimension count of Hom_C(C,C) are proved locally, and his §2.1 algebraically closed hypothesis is not imported.

§2e.1 projective-class basis for the particular algebra A_m
contents.reason: The A_m-specific projective basis is not a general theorem for finite-dimensional algebras; this pair proves separate exact and split group bases with explicit hypotheses.

contents.name: §2e.1 exact functors induce Laurent-linear Grothendieck operators
contents.reason: The source computes an operator for the special braid algebra A_m, not an adjoint pair under the general hypotheses of this page; that calculation belongs to the braid development.

contents.name: §2e.1 derived cone operators and braid relations
contents.reason: Derived cones and braid relations belong to the later braid and derived-functor developments; this page establishes only the group and pairing interface.

contents.name: Proposition 2.8, the resulting Burau representation
contents.reason: The Burau identification depends on the special A_m construction and categorical braid action, neither of which is a claim of this general Cartan-pairing page.
